svg.title: How to Time Travel in Delhi
svg.text: HOW TO TIME TRAVEL IN DELHI
Fifteen standing monuments, a thousand years of capitals, all within about 13 km of Raisina Hill — with real walking and driving routes, and objects reaching back to the 1st millennium BCE.
HOW FAR YOU GO · HOW FAR BACK YOU GET
By year founded (earliest on the left), distance from Raisina (left axis) and walking time (right axis). Dashed lines: older objects re-used or dug up at the site.
km from Raisina Hill, straight line (rings every 3 km)
year founded: earliest on the left, latest on the right

g.text: - - - rule of thumb: every km out ≈ 55 years back
least-squares fit, r = -0.77. South is older; the Mughal north breaks it.

svg.text: Ashokan Pillar · 3rd c. BCE · moved from Topra 1356
Painted Grey Ware sherds · 1st millennium BCE · dug up at Purana Qila
KEY · numbered along the suggested route, from 0
Firuz Shah Tughlaq; Ashokan Pillar 3rd c. BCE
Aibak, then Iltutmish; Iron Pillar c.400 CE
Anangpal II Tomar; Qila Rai Pithora 12th c.
Road distance, walk and drive times from Raisina via OpenStreetMap routing (FOSSGIS OSRM). *Drive times are free-flow: Delhi traffic typically makes them 2–3× longer.
THE SUGGESTED DAY · DRIVE SOUTH INTO THE PAST
0 Rashtrapati Bhavan → 1 Jantar Mantar → 2 Sis Ganj; walk Chandni Chowk to 3 Red Fort and 4 Jama Masjid (2.3 km, ~30 min); drive 5 Kotla → 6 Purana Qila → 7 Humayun → 8 Lodi → 9 Safdarjung → 10 Siri

→ 11 Tughlaqabad → 12 Jahanpanah → 13 Qutb; walk to 14 Lal Kot (0.9 km). Driving 56 km (~86 min free-flow, realistically 3+ hours); walking 3.2 km (~42 min). Broadly, you start in 1912 and end in c.1060.

Positions: Wikipedia/OpenStreetMap coordinates, local equirectangular projection centred on Raisina (28.6143° N, 77.1994° E), north up, 44 px/km. Jahanpanah is plotted at Bijay Mandal; Siri and Lal Kot at surviving wall sections.

Rings are straight-line distance at 4.5 km/h walking, after Galton’s isochronic passage chart (1881) and Bartholomew’s isochronic map (1914). Dates: ASI, UNESCO, Delhi SRDC and cited Wikipedia sources. Road and river data © OpenStreetMap contributors (ODbL).
